                    REPLY BRIEF OF LAMPASAS J11 LANDOWNERS


                                      Supportable Routes


       Based on the routes in contention and supported both in briefing and at hearing,

Lampasas J11 Landowners would not oppose Routes 296, 392, 410,572, 891 and CCG in

addition to Route 894. The record reflects minimal support for Route 487, other than from the

PUC Staff.


       The Commission should reject Route 487 and any other route that includes Link J11, as it

would unnecessarily impact a single, contiguous, and interconnected landscape and the

surrounding ranchlands and an otherwise pristine area of state parks abutting the Colorado River.

Together, these areas form one of the most intact, unspoiled, and carefully preserved landscapes

in Central Texas. The Commission should select a route that minimizes environmental impact,

avoids fragmentation of intact ranchland and wildlife habitat, and preserves the integrity of this
                                                 1
 landscape, including unnecessary new and intrusive crossings of the Colorado River. That

includes protecting not only individual features, but the continuity, context, and views that give

this area its significance.


        WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDEDRED, Lampasas J11 Landowners respectfully

request that Route 487, including Link J11, no longer be considered as any part of the route to be

considered for any transmission line, as it will have such a devastating and detrimental impact on

its property, as well as the crossing of an untouched pristine area of the Colorado Rivere. We

further recommend Route 894, or a similar alternative as listed above, avoiding Link J11, to be

selected and for such further and other relief as may be granted.


                                               Respectively submitted,


                                               _/s/Roger B. Borgelt _
